summary.one_liner: A 15-phase, in-progress networking curriculum that teaches the network stack from raw bytes using C and Python, with lessons on frames, TCP, TLS 1.3, kernel modules, eBPF/XDP, CNI plugins, VXLAN, and DDS.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is a structured course: 15 phases with 289 planned lessons, of which only three sample lessons (P1.02 endianness, P2.06 ARP, P3.02 Internet checksum) are written and complete. Each lesson is meant to follow the same six-section layout (Problem, Theory, Math/Spec, Code, Tests, Exercises). The stated goals include hand-building an Ethernet frame sent through a raw socket, a userspace TCP/IP stack on a TUN/TAP device, a TLS 1.3 client handshake, a Netfilter kernel module, an XDP SYN-flood dropper, a Python CNI bridge plugin, a VXLAN overlay, and a DDS publisher that interoperates with Cyclone DDS. The repo includes a lint script that checks lesson structure, a top-level Makefile, and tox for Python tests. Most kernel-level lessons require root on Linux.
use_cases: learn networking by implementing protocols from scratch
write a raw Ethernet frame through a raw socket
build a userspace TCP/IP stack on a TUN device
study TLS 1.3 handshake byte by byte
follow a structured networking course with exercises
practice eBPF/XDP and kernel module networking
notable: Each lesson follows a fixed six-section format (Problem, Theory, Math/Spec, Code, Tests, Exercises) enforced by a lint script
Builds a userspace TCP/IP stack on a Linux TUN/TAP device, aiming to curl a real HTTPS site
Covers kernel-level topics including a Netfilter LKM, XDP SYN-flood dropping, and AF_XDP
Includes a DDS publisher lesson meant to interoperate with Eclipse Cyclone DDS
Ships with a setup script for an Ubuntu 24.04 VM
caveats: Only 3 of about 289 lessons are written; the rest are planned, and the README says the curriculum is in progress
Most kernel-module, TUN/TAP, eBPF, and namespace lessons require root on a Linux machine, and the README recommends a disposable VM
Targets Linux; the prerequisites assume Ubuntu 24.04 for the setup script
